messages:
eva_eval: nightly-eval flagged a regression on the INT8 calibration sweep for rwd-llama3-13b-v2. f1/drop looks small overall but we have a consistent failure mode: ~6% EM drop on the 'docqa' prompt set since the calib update last night. :eyes:

anna_ml: ugh. did the nightly pick up a different quant table? any change in the per-head scales or clipping?

sam_runtime: deploy-bot says the quant-lib bump (v2.9.1 -> v2.10.0) landed in the calibrate job at 02:12 UTC. logs attached in CI but gist: https://ci.internal/runs/98765

deploy-bot: nightly-eval 2027-03-15 02:30 UTC finished. models tested: rwd-llama3-13b-v2 int8/float fp8/int8-calib. Report: https://reports.internal/nightly/1818345600

lee_infra: quick summary from logs: calibration produced a new scale-table file calib/llama3-13b/2027-03-15/scale_table.npy. Size differs by ~2% vs previous. Also saw a few NaN warnings during per-layer histogram smoothing (line ~438).

anna_ml: copy of failing prompt+gold for reproduction: "Given the excerpt, what is the author's main argument?" gold: "regulatory oversight is insufficient" model int8-gen: "the author argues that oversight is necessary" -> paraphrase mismatch but EM wrong. This pattern repeats on extraction-type QA where short spans are needed.

marta: can we run a focused sweep: reproduce with the exact quant table used last night, then swap in the previous table and re-run eval. If repro, bisect quant-lib bump. Who owns?

sam_runtime: i'll run repro on a dedicated node. command i'll use: ```python tools/eval_harness.py --model rwd-llama3-13b-v2 --quant int8 --scale-table calib/llama3-13b/2027-03-15/scale_table.npy --prompts evalsets/docqa --out /tmp/repro.json``` i'll also run with the prior scale table `calib/.../2027-03-14/scale_table.npy`

eva_eval: thanks. also add --seed 42 and --kv-cache-stats so we can compare attention norm distributions. we saw divergence in topk token probs for short-span answers.

lee_infra: note: earlier change in v2.10.0 disabled per-head symmetric-clipping fallback in one path. could be related. i'll stand by to bisect if repro succeeds.

anna_ml: if repro shows drop only with new table, we should run a narrow head-by-head injection test to find which layers/scales cause the EM loss. i can prepare a script that replaces scales per-layer and runs the 200-sample docqa subset.

sam_runtime: repro started (node g5-16x). ETA ~22 minutes. logging to /var/tmp/ci-98765/repro.log. ping when done.

marta: prioritize: 1) repro and confirm delta 2) bisect quant-lib if needed 3) temporary rollback of nightly calib job to previous scale table (low-risk) 4) add assertion in nightly eval harness to flag >3% EM drop on extraction sets so we catch earlier. assign: sam runtime, anna head tests, lee infra bisect, eva track metrics.

eva_eval: noted. i'll open a short runbook and add the failing prompt examples + summary to the incident tracker: https://incidents.internal/IN-2027-045

sam_runtime: repro finished. results: with 2027-03-15 table EM=72.1, with 2027-03-14 table EM=78.3, FP baseline float EM=79.0. attaching diff excerpts: ```diff --repro
- EM 78.3 -> 72.1 (int8)
- topk token prob KL increased for span endpoints (mean KL 0.24 -> 0.62)
```

anna_ml: ok that's pretty conclusive it's scale-table related. starting head-swap tests now. script will try replacing scales for layers 22-26 first (previously these heads had max var shifts).

lee_infra: starting quick bisect on quant-lib commits between v2.9.1 and v2.10.0 to see if any change touched smoothing/clipping code. parallelizing on 4 nodes.

marta: thanks team. keep updates light in this thread. if we confirm causality we'll do the rollback and a hotfix to restore symmetric-clipping fallback until we have a proper fix. :thumbsup:

eva_eval: small note: add the evaluation seed and exact tokenizer version to the nightly report to make triage easier next time. saw tokenization drift in a past incident that masked calibration issues.

sam_runtime: agreed. I'll append tokenizer and seed metadata to the next nightly job config.

(reacts: anna_ml :eyes:, sam_runtime :rocket:, marta :white_check_mark:)
